official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 calculator boundary revisions
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's calculator guidance updated 11 March 2026 changed River Camel and River Eden calculator inputs to reflect revised catchment boundaries and WINEP treatment-work assumptions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Poole credit scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's 15 June 2026 Poole guidance states nutrient credits mitigate nitrogen for qualifying development in the Poole Harbour SPA and Ramsar catchment and are part of, not a substitute for, the planning process.

official_measurement_examples.name: Tees credit scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's 15 June 2026 Tees guidance applies to qualifying accommodation development in the Teesmouth catchment and requires the planning-application context to be retained.

official_measurement_examples.name: Continuous sales not unlimited approval
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England sells credits continuously in current scheme areas, but availability or purchase of credits does not itself determine the planning application or all Habitats Regulations requirements.

official_measurement_examples.name: Nutrient budget role
official_measurement_examples.fact: The official calculators estimate a proposal-specific nutrient budget to support planning and HRA evidence; calculator output is not a general parcel suitability score.

official_measurement_examples.name: Natural England role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's May 2026 clarification describes its role as supporting sustainable development and strategic mitigation while planning authorities retain their statutory decision-making functions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Catchment specificity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Nutrient neutrality requirements and calculator assumptions are catchment- and nutrient-specific and must not be transferred between protected sites without authoritative evidence.

official_measurement_examples.name: HRA separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Nutrient mitigation evidence, credit certificates, nutrient budgets, appropriate assessment and planning permission are distinct steps and none alone establishes parcel development capacity.

core_rules: nutrient-neutrality catchment membership is not automatic planning refusal
absence from one historic catchment map is not proof nutrient neutrality is irrelevant
current calculator versions and revised catchment boundaries take precedence over stale copies
nutrient budget calculation is not planning permission
nutrient credit availability is not planning permission
a nutrient credit certificate does not replace Habitats Regulations assessment
Poole Harbour and Tees credit rules must not be transferred to unrelated catchments
nitrogen and phosphorus requirements must not be interchanged
wastewater-treatment assumptions must retain their implementation dates
private mitigation and Natural England credits must not be assumed interchangeable without scheme evidence
Natural England mitigation activity is distinct from the local planning authority decision
appropriate assessment remains distinct from nutrient budget arithmetic
nutrient mitigation does not determine land ownership access rights or infrastructure capacity
historic calculator outputs must retain version catchment and treatment-work assumptions
no parcel nutrient-neutrality clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
